extracted.intended_audience: Poynter staff, faculty, contributors, guest instructors, event participants, and donors; journalists and journalism students who engage with Poynter
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational code of ethics and conduct for a nonprofit journalism school/publisher covering core journalistic values, business practices with funders, event code of conduct, and staff nonpartisanship. Intended to guide Poynter employees, contributors, instructors and event attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: We do our best to make sure that everything we publish is accurate and true to the facts. This ranges from the easily confirmed, e.g. the spelling of names, to the nuanced and more debatable, e.g. characterizations of political initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain high standards of reporting, writing and editing to produce work that is as error-free as possible; create and edit to anticipate problem areas, reduce mistakes and correct them quickly and transparently; provide timely responses, clear corrections and prominent acknowledgments that a mistake was made and addressed; credit authors and creators; apply appropriate scrutiny to work by staff and contributors to prevent plagiarism; do not intentionally mislead with words or images; do not deliberately deceive in newsgathering; encourage best possible work within resource limits; value accuracy over timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: We are an independent, 501(c)(3), nonpartisan, nonprofit journalism education and research institute. We manage our conflicts of interest and seek to remain free of influences that might interfere with journalism or teaching that is accurate, fair, transparent, professional and helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing about our teaching, a Poynter event or a topic that’s funded by a grant or other contribution, retain editorial control and disclose the relationship; retain independence over content created on subjects supported by funders; faculty and staff must not enter relationships that compromise the Institute’s work; gifts must not influence coverage or teaching; return gifts over $50 and donate unreturnable gifts; business partnerships do not influence news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter must cultivate relationships throughout the journalism and technology community to fulfill its mission — these relationships make us smarter, more relevant and more capable of supporting journalism and democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace ties to organizations and individuals for advice, participation in courses, content and financial support; rely on partners for program support while retaining independent control over editorial content; consult partners for expertise and sometimes share draft agendas and tentative speaker lists when appropriate; partners may teach if subject-matter experts, but Poynter faculty will coach them and Poynter makes final determination of teaching content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to act justly, to respect people and their privacy, to present different points of view and to minimize harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge relevant points of view and represent them even‑handedly; reach out to subjects for comment; provide accessible ways to challenge Poynter (webstaff@poynter.org) and respond promptly and with purpose; maintain a non-discriminatory admission policy for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: We shine a light on our own journalistic processes, explaining how and why we make decisions and disclosing relevant information that may have influenced or affected our decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose ownership (e.g., Poynter’s ownership of The Tampa Bay Times) and relevant business relationships; label all non-news content clearly as “Sponsored Content” or “From the Institute”; label ads that promote sponsored content as “Advertising”; label funder-supported pages/content within or immediately below the header image; label sponsored newsletter items as “sponsored post” or “a note from our sponsor.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence for accepting contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with a donor, granting organization or corporate sponsor, Poynter’s development staff and administration will research the funder’s mission, values and history of giving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the type of support offered and the teaching and outcomes expected; consult employees responsible for carrying out funded teaching throughout vetting; after agreements, employees must alert administration if funder requests or demands do not serve Poynter’s mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileges routinely granted to funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter routinely grants certain privileges to funders as part of support arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical privileges include: logo on marketing and teaching collateral including advertising and syllabi; invitation for representatives to attend teaching events; a small, proportionate amount of time to welcome and address the audience (clearly labeled as a message from the sponsor); sharing draft agendas and tentative speaker lists when funders have subject-matter expertise; representatives of funding organizations may teach if experts, but Poynter faculty coach them and Poynter determines final teaching content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of funder support and sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter will prominently list funders who support teaching events and disclose sponsorship in promotional materials and on teaching agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When industry groups or for-profit companies sponsor teaching, disclose sponsorship and sign an agreement giving Poynter independence and control over teaching; when funders underwrite content areas or newsletters, label the page/content and newsletter items appropriately; provide transparency about travel/lodging support paid by funders and offer alternatives for participants who decline such support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting funders with concerning histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain funders require an extra level of vigilance, e.g., funders with a history of anti-democratic activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poynter’s president or vice president will personally review proposed programs supported by such funders by asking questions including: How does the program support development of journalists or democratic systems? Does the potential outcome outweigh validating an organization whose past actions undermine journalism? What will recipients do with the training? What other options exist for training journalists under the funder’s influence? What additional guarantees exist that teachers will proceed without interference? What will happen if teachers criticize the funder during training? How will Poynter’s brand be used by the funder?

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift policy (specific threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter faculty and staff do not allow gifts from sources, students, or vendors to influence our coverage or our teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return any gift worth more than $50; gifts that cannot be returned are donated to an appropriate charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives of the Poynter Institute avoid the public expression of political opinion and public involvement in the political process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make political contributions or work on campaigns; do not sign online petitions, post yard signs, or participate in political marches; avoid expressing political views on social media (sharing news stories is allowed but take care not to be seen as endorsing or opposing figures or positions); avoid snarky commentary; employees may vote privately but keep votes to themselves; policy applies to full-time staff, correspondents, adjunct faculty, and interns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discriminatory admission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants to the Poynter Institute shall not be denied admission on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, marital status, national origin, disability, or sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit institutional commitment to nondiscrimination in admissions to Poynter programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event Code of Conduct: Expected behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat everyone with respect; participate while acknowledging everyone deserves respectful treatment and the right to enjoy their experience without fear of harassment or discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be considerate, respectful and collaborative; refrain from demeaning, discriminatory or harassing behavior and speech; immediately inform Poynter Vice President of Business & Finance Jessi Navarro (in person, phone 727-337-7131, or jnavarro@poynter.org) if you observe or experience unwelcome/offensive behavior; seek permission before quoting anyone involved in a program or sharing presented materials; be respectful to public patrons and staff at events open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event Code of Conduct: Unacceptable behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Unacceptable behavior includes, but is not limited to, intimidating, threatening, harassing, abusive, discriminatory, derogatory, demeaning or disorderly conduct; or possession, use or distribution of any illegal substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexually harassing conduct can be by a person of the same or opposite sex; Poynter reserves the right in its sole discretion to determine what constitutes unacceptable behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event Code of Conduct: Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Unacceptable behavior will not be tolerated whether by attendees, media, speakers or venue staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone asked to stop unacceptable behavior must comply immediately; Poynter may take any action it deems appropriate, up to and including immediate expulsion without warning from the event and without refund of any associated fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and assistance procedures for incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: If you witness or are subject to unacceptable behavior, immediately notify security staff and/or Poynter Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer Jessi Navarro (phone 727-337-7131 or jnavarro@poynter.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also notify appropriate law enforcement if necessary; Poynter will assist participants to contact venue security or local law enforcement, provide escorts, or otherwise assist those experiencing unacceptable behavior to feel safe for the duration of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission before quoting or sharing presented materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek permission from anyone involved in a program before quoting them or sharing materials that may have been presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required behavior for attendees and guest instructors to respect presenters’ rights and event expectations.
